title: Say a word until it means nothing

lines.text: Say the word spoon out loud, over and over. Spoon. Spoon. Spoon. Spoon. Spoon. Spoon.
Does it still sound like a real word?
That strange feeling has a name. Semantic satiation.
The term was coined in 1962 by psychologist Leon Jakobovits James, at McGill University.
One idea is that repeating a word makes the brain's response to it weaker each time.
The sound keeps coming, but the meaning stops arriving.
It only takes a few seconds of repetition to happen.
Now try it with your own name.

sources.claim: Semantic satiation: term coined by Leon Jakobovits James in his 1962 McGill dissertation; repetition for several seconds; possibly a form of reactive inhibition

publish.title: Say a Word Until It Means Nothing 🥄
publish.description: Repeat any word for a few seconds and it turns into noise. It's called semantic satiation. Try it.
